intro: Vietnam is a long S-shaped country running about 1,650 km along the South China Sea, from mountains on the Chinese border to the Mekong Delta.

chapters.title: Two rice baskets on a pole
text: Vietnamese people describe their country as two rice baskets on a carrying pole: the Red River Delta in the north and the Mekong Delta in the south, joined by a narrow middle that is only about 50 km wide at its thinnest.
The Annamite mountains run down the west. Fansipan, at 3,143 m, is the highest peak in Indochina.

chapters.title: Bays and caves
text: Hạ Long Bay has around 1,600 limestone islands rising from green water. Sơn Đoòng in Phong Nha-Kẻ Bàng is the world's largest known cave by volume, with its own jungle and clouds inside.

chapters.title: Climate
text: The north has cool winters and hot summers; the south is hot all year with wet and dry seasons. Typhoons hit the central coast most years.
